sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Physalis crassifolia is a rhizomatous perennial, sometimes suffrutescent, usually 10–40 cm tall and reaching about 1 m. It grows on rocky slopes, mesas, ravines and roadsides of the south-western United States and north-western Mexico.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The ovate to deltoid leaves are about 0.8–3.3 cm long, sometimes longer. The yellow flowers have brownish markings. The inflated fruiting calyx surrounds a berry.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No safe food use was documented for this species; do not infer edibility from that of other Physalis.
